stories.title: See today's feast, saints and tone
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want to see today's feast or saint, the week and the tone, so that I know what the Church is celebrating today.
criteria: Shows the day's title, week name and tone
Shows a badge for major feasts
Uses the Antiochian (Greek) tradition on the New calendar

stories.title: Read the day's scripture readings
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want to read the day's Epistle and Gospel in full, so that I can follow the readings at home or before Liturgy.
criteria: Lists every reading for the day, grouped by service
Each reading expands to show the full verse text

stories.title: Read the lives of the saints
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want to read the lives of the saints commemorated today, so that I can learn from their example.
criteria: Lists the saints commemorated today
Each saint's life expands to show the full story
Saints' life text is sanitized before it's displayed

stories.title: Know today's fasting rule
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want a clear fasting rule for each day, so that I know which foods to avoid and which are allowed.
criteria: Each day maps to one FastingRule (strict, wine only, wine & oil, fish, meat fast, fast-free, no fast)
A color-coded card lists foods to avoid and foods allowed
Checked against tricky days such as Cheesefare, Lazarus Saturday, Holy Saturday and Christmas Eve
Automated tests cover every fasting code
stories.notes: Orthocal follows strict typikon practice. The app should remind people to follow their priest's guidance.

stories.title: Look up any date
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want to move between days and pick any date, so that I can plan for upcoming feasts and fasts.
criteria: Prev and Next buttons move one day at a time
A date picker jumps to any date
Links like ?date=2026-12-25 can be shared
Impossible dates show a clear error message

stories.title: Readings match the Archdiocese
stories.story: As an Antiochian Orthodox Christian, I want the app to show the same daily readings as antiochian.org, so that I read what is read in church.
criteria: Only the Divine Liturgy's Epistle and Gospel (no Vespers or Matins readings)
A saint's or feast's readings replace the weekday ones; on Sundays the Sunday Gospel stays
References written like antiochian.org, e.g. "St. Paul's Letter to the Galatians 1:11-19"
Checked against 47 days on antiochian.org (all matched)

stories.title: Listen to the readings and lives of the saints
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want the app to read the scripture readings and saints' lives aloud, so that I can listen while driving, cooking or resting my eyes.
criteria: A Listen button on every reading and every saint's life
Uses the device's own built-in voices only, never an online AI voice service
Pause, resume, stop, reading speed and voice choice

stories.title: Automatic build and tests on every push
stories.story: As the developer, I want GitHub to build the app and run the tests every time I push, so that I find out right away if something breaks.
criteria: A GitHub Actions workflow runs `mvn verify` on every push and pull request
The README shows a build status badge
The packaged .jar can be downloaded from each run

stories.title: Get permission to use the Archdiocese parish directory
stories.story: As the developer, I want the Archdiocese's blessing to use its parish directory, so that the parish finder has complete, accurate data.
criteria: Email sent to archdiocese@antiochian.org (sent 2026-10-22)
Reply received, with any conditions noted here
Agreed way to receive the data (export or feed)
stories.notes: Until permission comes through, build and test the parish finder with a few parishes entered by hand.

stories.title: Store parishes in a database
stories.story: As the developer, I want parishes stored in a database, so that the app can search them quickly.
criteria: Spring Data JPA with H2 while developing (PostgreSQL later)
A Parish entity: name, address, phone, website, diocese, rite, latitude, longitude
A few sample parishes loaded at startup, starting with Saints Constantine and Helen in Carrollton, TX

stories.title: Find parishes near me
stories.story: As someone looking for a church, I want to see the Antiochian parishes nearest to me, so that I can find one to visit.
criteria: Asks the browser for my location (only with my permission)
Lists parishes sorted by distance, in miles
Works without location by falling back to a city or ZIP search

stories.title: Search parishes by city, state or ZIP
stories.story: As someone travelling, I want to search for parishes by city, state or ZIP code, so that I can find a church where I'll be.
criteria: A search box accepts a city, state or ZIP
Results show name, city and distance
A clear message appears when nothing is found

stories.title: See parish details and get directions
stories.story: As someone looking for a church, I want to see a parish's address, phone and website and get directions, so that I can contact or visit it.
criteria: A details view shows address, phone, website and diocese
Phone and website are tappable links
A Directions button opens the address in a maps app

stories.title: Filter parishes by diocese
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want to filter parishes by diocese, so that I can see the churches in my region.
criteria: A diocese filter lists all dioceses
Filtering works together with the location and text search

stories.title: Sign up and log in
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to create an account and log in, so that the app can remember my parish and preferences.
criteria: Sign up with email and password; passwords stored hashed (BCrypt)
Log in returns a JWT token used for later requests
Log out, and clear error messages for wrong passwords

stories.title: Choose my home parish
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to choose my home parish, so that I see its events and news first.
criteria: Pick a home parish from the parish finder
The home parish appears on my dashboard

stories.title: Bookmark saints and feasts
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to bookmark saints and feasts, so that I can come back to them and be reminded of their days.
criteria: A bookmark button on each saint and feast
A My Bookmarks page lists them with their dates

stories.title: Parish admin role
stories.story: As a parish administrator, I want permission to manage my parish's information and events, so that parishioners always see accurate details.
criteria: Roles: member, parish admin, site admin
Parish admins can edit only their own parish

stories.title: Sign in with Google
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that I don't need another password.
criteria: A "Continue with Google" button on the sign-in page
The first Google sign-in creates an account from my verified Google email and name
If an account with the same email already exists, Google is linked to it
The button only appears once Google keys are set in secrets.properties

stories.title: Sign in with Apple
stories.story: As an iPhone user, I want to sign in with my Apple ID, so that I can sign in quickly and keep my email private if I choose.
criteria: A "Continue with Apple" button on the sign-in page
Works with Apple's "Hide My Email" addresses
The button only appears once Apple keys are set in secrets.properties
Tested end to end once the app is online over HTTPS
stories.notes: Apple requires a paid Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year) and a real HTTPS web address (it doesn't allow localhost), so this can only be tested after the app is online (#25). The App Store also requires Sign in with Apple in any iPhone app that offers Google sign-in.

stories.title: Strong password rules
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want the app to require a strong password, so that my account is hard to break into.
criteria: At least 12 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a symbol
Rejects passwords containing my email name, or a common word with numbers added (like "Password2026!")
The sign-up page shows a live checklist of the rules as I type
Passwords are stored only as BCrypt hashes, never as plain text
5 wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes

stories.title: Add my phone number
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to optionally add my phone number, so that I can receive sign-in codes by text message.
criteria: Phone number is optional at sign-up and can be added, changed or removed later
US numbers can be typed in any common format; other countries start with +
The number is confirmed with a 6-digit code sent by text before it can be used

stories.title: Two-step verification by email or text
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to turn on two-step verification, so that someone who learns my password still can't get into my account.
criteria: Choose Off, Email or Text message on my account page
Only a verified email or phone number can be chosen
After the correct password, sign-in asks for a 6-digit code sent to that email or phone
Codes expire after 10 minutes, allow 5 tries, and can be re-sent after 30 seconds

stories.title: Reset a forgotten password
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to reset my password if I forget it, so that I don't lose my account.
criteria: A "Forgot password?" link on the sign-in page
A reset code or link is sent to my verified email
The new password must follow the strong password rules

stories.title: Send real emails and text messages
stories.story: As the developer, I want codes delivered by real email and text messages, so that people outside my computer can use two-step verification.
criteria: Email through an SMTP service (Gmail for testing, a sending service when live)
Text messages through Twilio
Settings kept in secrets.properties, never committed to GitHub
stories.notes: Until this is set up, codes are printed in the VS Code terminal (development mode). Twilio charges per text, and US numbers need a one-time registration (A2P 10DLC).

stories.title: Customize my profile
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to add a profile photo, my patron saint, my name day and my home parish, so that the app feels like mine.
criteria: Upload a JPEG or PNG photo, cropped to a square; remove it any time
Photos are re-saved by the server, which strips hidden data such as GPS location
Save my patron saint, name day and home parish
On my name day, the home page wishes me a happy name day

stories.title: Choose text size and dark mode
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to choose a larger text size and a dark theme, so that the app is comfortable to read, including in church or at night.
criteria: Text size: Normal, Large or Larger
Theme: match my device, Light or Dark
Settings are saved to my account and applied on every page

stories.title: Read and download the day's service texts
stories.story: As a chanter or parishioner, I want to read the day's service texts (Vespers, Orthros, Divine Liturgy) in the app or download them as PDFs, so that I can follow or prepare for the services.
criteria: Each day links to the Archdiocese's Online Liturgical Guide
Permission from the Archdiocese's Department of Liturgics to show its texts in the app
With permission: the day's PDFs open in an in-app viewer, with a Download button
stories.notes: The Archdiocese publishes these texts at antiochian.org/liturgicday. The texts are its own approved translations, and the list of each day's files comes from a private, login-protected feed, so we link to the guide until we have permission.

stories.title: Move around the app with tabs
stories.story: As a user, I want a tab bar at the bottom of the screen, like Instagram's, so that I can jump between the main parts of the app with one tap.
criteria: Four tabs: Home (the default), Bible, Prayers and Profile
The current tab is highlighted
The Profile tab shows my photo when I'm signed in, and the sign-in page when I'm not

stories.title: Read the Orthodox Bible
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want the whole Bible in the app, with the Orthodox Old Testament, so that I can read any chapter at any time.
criteria: Old Testament from the Septuagint, including Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach and the Maccabees, with Orthodox Psalm numbering
New Testament in the King James Version, matching the daily readings
Books in Orthodox order; chapter by chapter, with previous and next
Continue reading where I left off, and listen to any chapter
Only public-domain translations

stories.title: Pray with a prayer book
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want a prayer book in the app, so that I can keep my morning and evening prayers wherever I am.
criteria: Beginning (Trisagion), morning and evening prayers, the Creed, meals, the Theotokos, the Jesus Prayer, before Scripture, Communion, the departed, protection, Lent and Pascha
Psalms come from the Bible tab's Septuagint text
Listen to a whole section
Prayers kept in a data file, so they can be corrected without changing code
stories.notes: The Archdiocese's own prayer book translations are copyrighted; they could be added with its permission.

stories.title: Read church news
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want to read Archdiocese and parish news, so that I stay connected to the life of the Church.
criteria: A news list with title, date and summary
Admins can create, edit and delete articles

stories.title: See my parish's events
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to see my parish's upcoming events and schedule changes, so that I don't miss services.
criteria: Upcoming events listed by date
Parish admins can post updates such as "Vespers moved to 6:30 PM"

stories.title: Pray with the prayer library
stories.story: As an Orthodox Christian, I want morning, evening and occasional prayers in the app, so that I can pray wherever I am.
criteria: Prayers grouped by time of day and occasion
Readable on a phone screen
Only texts we have permission to use

stories.title: Learn about the dioceses and ministries
stories.story: As someone new to the Church, I want pages about the Archdiocese, its dioceses and ministries, so that I understand how it's organised.
criteria: A page for each diocese with its bishop and parishes
Ministries and About pages

stories.title: A modern app screen (React)
stories.story: As a user, I want a fast, modern app screen, so that the app is pleasant to use on any device.
criteria: A React (Vite) frontend replaces the preview page
Works well on phone, tablet and desktop screen sizes

stories.title: Fast loading with caching
stories.story: As a user, I want each day to load instantly, so that the app feels quick even on a slow connection.
criteria: Each day's calendar data is cached until midnight Central time
The app still works if Orthocal is briefly offline for cached days

stories.title: Morning summary notification
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want a 6 AM summary of the day's feast, fast and parish events, so that I start each day prepared.
criteria: A scheduled job builds the summary at 6:00 AM
Delivered by email first, then push notifications
Can be turned off in my settings

stories.title: Install the app on my phone or computer
stories.story: As a user, I want to install the app on my home screen, so that I can open it like any other app.
criteria: The web app is an installable PWA
Android and iOS apps built with Capacitor

stories.title: Put the app online
stories.story: As a user, I want to open the app from anywhere, so that I don't need the developer's computer to be running.
criteria: Backend, database and frontend hosted online
A public web address for the app

stories.title: Choose the app's style
stories.story: As a user, I want to choose how the app looks from Orthodox-inspired styles, so that it feels like mine and not like every other app.
criteria: Five styles: Illuminated manuscript, Byzantine mosaic, Candlelit vigil, Holy Mountain and Liturgical seasons
Each style has a light and a dark version
Choose a style when creating an account, and change it any time in Profile
Liturgical seasons follows the Church year, like the colors of the vestments

stories.title: Tabs remember where I was
stories.story: As a user, I want each tab to stay exactly where I left it, so that switching tabs never loses my place or reloads the page.
criteria: Switching tabs keeps each tab's page, scroll position and open sections
Nothing reloads when coming back to a tab
Pulling down at the top of a page refreshes it
Tapping the current tab again goes back to that tab's first page

stories.title: Pray for the Archdiocese each day
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want a different diocese, hierarch or ministry to pray for each day, so that over the year I pray for the whole Archdiocese.
criteria: A "Pray today for" card that changes every day
Shown on the Church tab and on Home
Includes a short commemoration in the style of the Church's litanies

stories.title: Two-step verification with an authenticator app
stories.story: As a user, I want my second sign-in step to use an authenticator app, so that my account is protected without depending on email or text messages.
criteria: Set up by scanning a QR code (or typing a key) in Profile
Works with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, the iPhone Passwords app and others
One-time backup codes in case the phone is lost
Email and text codes are only offered where the server can really send them

stories.title: Stay signed in until I sign out
stories.story: As a user, I want to stay signed in until I choose to sign out, so that I don't have to sign in again every time I open the app.
criteria: Still signed in after the server restarts, and after weeks away
Only Sign out signs you out
The long-lasting sign-in cookie can't be forged, and page scripts can't read it

stories.title: See who has an account
stories.story: As the app's administrator, I want to see how many people have accounts and how to reach them, so that I can look after the people using the app.
criteria: A Members page that only administrators can open
The number of accounts, and each member's name, email, phone number, how they sign in and when they joined
Download the list as a spreadsheet
Passwords are never shown: only one-way hashes of them are stored

stories.title: Choose my patron saint's feast day
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want to choose my patron saint's feast day as a month and a day, so that the app wishes me a happy name day every year.
criteria: The feast day is chosen right under the patron saint in Profile
A month and a day, with no year
A greeting on Home on that day

stories.title: Choose a reading voice
stories.story: As a listener, I want a short choice of clear voices, so that reading aloud sounds good without sorting through dozens of voices.
criteria: Three voices: David, Mark and Zira on Windows, and three American voices on other devices
No novelty voices
Plain Listen, Pause, Resume and Stop buttons

stories.title: Read the app's privacy policy
stories.story: As a user, I want to read what the app keeps about me and why, so that I can trust it with my account.
criteria: A plain page at /privacy
Linked from the sign-in page, Profile and Google's sign-in screen

stories.title: Two-step verification after launch
stories.story: As a user, I want an optional second step when signing in, so that a stolen password alone can't open my account.
criteria: Decide which methods to offer (authenticator app, text message, email)
Optional for each person
stories.notes: Built in October 2026 (an authenticator app, and codes by text or email), then taken out on 2026-10-24 until after launch. The last version is in commit a65d129.

stories.title: Get a daily notification at a time I choose
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want a notification each day with the feast or saint, the fast and the readings, at a time I choose, so that I start each day prepared.
criteria: Turned on per device in Profile, and off again just as easily
I choose the time; it comes at that time where I live
Works on iPhone (Home Screen app), Android and computers

stories.title: A cheerful greeting on my name day
stories.story: As a parishioner, I want a cheerful notification on my patron saint's feast day, so that my name day feels celebrated.
criteria: Sent when my patron saint and their feast day are filled in on Profile
On unless I turn it off
A feast on February 29th is kept on the 28th in other years
